finding.claim: Broken authorization on the ban endpoint. require_admin() denies access by calling abort(403), which raises an HTTPException. ban() wraps that call in try/except Exception, logs a warning, and then falls through to do_ban(uid). Any authenticated non-admin can ban arbitrary users. The unban route has no try/except and does enforce the check, so the two routes are inconsistent.
finding.source: Any authenticated non-admin user sending POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban with an arbitrary uid

trace.note: Route /admin/users/<uid>/ban accepts POST, and uid is attacker-controlled
require_admin(g.user) is called for a non-admin, so abort(403) at line 11 raises werkzeug HTTPException
except Exception catches the HTTPException, because HTTPException subclasses Exception
Only a warning is logged. The handler does not re-raise or return
Execution continues to do_ban(uid) and returns ok=True

finding.guards_checked: require_admin checks is_admin and aborts with 403, but the surrounding except Exception swallows the abort. No before_request hook, decorator or other auth middleware exists in the file. do_ban has no internal check, and it is a stub. unban correctly lets the 403 propagate. Minor additional issue: line 19 logs g.user name, and a missing g.user would also be swallowed here.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) aborts with 403 for non-admins, but the abort is swallowed by except Exception at admin.py:18. There is no before_request hook, decorator or other middleware in the file.
